visual: Compact evergreen shrub with dense, small spine-tipped dark green leaves, white urn-shaped flowers and large vivid red berries from autumn into winter.
water: Keep consistently moist, especially while establishing and when grown in sunnier positions or containers.
soil: Moist but well-drained acidic to neutral soil.
soilWarning: Avoid alkaline or chalky soil. Female plants require a compatible male Gaultheria nearby for reliable berry production.
prune: Requires little pruning; remove damaged growth and lightly shape after flowering if needed. Unwanted suckers can be removed to restrict spread.
toxicity: Fruit is ornamental and should not be eaten. Wear gloves when handling if sensitive.
resilience: Very cold hardy and generally pest-free; may be susceptible to honey fungus where the disease is already present.
uses: Autumn and winter berry display, acid border, woodland planting, coastal garden and containers.
uncertain: The supplied label 'Signal' is a recognised synonym; RHS accepts Gaultheria mucronata 'Signaal' as the cultivar name.

visual: Low clump-forming evergreen perennial with broad leathery green leaves that develop rich maroon-red winter colouring, topped by vivid magenta-pink bell-shaped flowers in early spring.
water: Water regularly while establishing; mature plants tolerate some drought but perform best with moderate moisture.
soil: Humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid prolonged waterlogging and extreme hot, dry conditions. Early flowers can occasionally be damaged by hard frost.
prune: Remove faded flower spikes and damaged or tired foliage as required.
resilience: Cold hardy and reasonably drought tolerant once established; may be affected by vine weevil, slugs, snails and leaf spot.
uses: Ground cover, shady border, banks and slopes, coastal planting, underplanting shrubs and containers.

visual: Dense, bushy clump-forming perennial with fresh green pointed leaves and numerous slender upright spikes of deep red flowers from midsummer well into autumn.
water: Keep reliably moist during active growth, particularly during hot dry periods.
soil: Moist, humus-rich soil; tolerates acid, neutral or alkaline conditions and heavier ground.
soilWarning: Does not enjoy prolonged drought. Allow enough space for the steadily expanding clump.
prune: Cut old flowering stems and foliage back after flowering or before fresh growth begins in spring.
toxicity: Sap and plant material may irritate skin, and ingestion may cause mild stomach upset. Wear gloves when handling if sensitive.
resilience: Extremely cold hardy, vigorous and generally pest- and disease-free; established plants cope particularly well in moisture-retentive soils.
uses: Perennial border, wildlife garden, mass planting, cottage garden and naturalistic planting.
uncertain: Bonfire is the trade designation; 'Bokrafire' is the cultivar name.
RHS now places the taxon under Bistorta amplexicaulis; Persicaria amplexicaulis remains widely used in horticultural trade.
H7 follows RHS data for Bistorta/Persicaria amplexicaulis because a separate cultivar-specific hardiness rating for 'Bokrafire' was not published.

visual: Compact clump-forming perennial with dramatic scalloped leaves maturing to rich burgundy-brown, each outlined by a narrow lime-green to golden margin, with sprays of small white flowers in late spring.
water: Keep moderately and evenly moist, especially while establishing and when grown in containers.
soil: Reasonably fertile, moist but well-drained neutral soil.
soilWarning: Avoid persistent waterlogging and severe drying. An organic mulch helps maintain even root moisture.
prune: Remove faded flower stems and dead or damaged leaves as required.
resilience: Very cold hardy and generally disease-free; vine weevil can be troublesome, particularly in containers.
uses: Shady border, foliage planting, ground cover, edging, shrub underplanting and patio containers.

visual: Compact bushy sage with aromatic bright green foliage and abundant two-lipped bicoloured flowers, white with striking bright pink lips, over a long summer and autumn flowering season.
water: Water regularly while establishing, then moderately during prolonged dry spells. Allow the soil surface to dry slightly between waterings.
soil: Light, moderately fertile, well-drained soil; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Excellent winter drainage is important. Avoid heavy waterlogged soil, particularly during cold weather.
prune: Deadhead during summer to prolong flowering. Cut back and reshape in spring once strong new growth is visible rather than pruning hard in autumn.
resilience: Heat and drought tolerant once established and highly attractive to pollinators; winter wet is often more damaging than cold.
uses: Sunny border, wildlife garden, Mediterranean-style planting, gravel garden, coastal planting and patio container.
uncertain: The supplied name 'Magicalo Mississippi' resolves to Salvia Magical® Mississippi.
Walter Blom Plants lists Magical® Mississippi at 40–50 cm tall, flowering May to October and within USDA zones 6–9.
The Dutch VARB plant-name register places Magical Mississippi under Salvia jamensis; modern RHS usage for this group is Salvia × jamensis.
H5 follows the RHS hardiness rating for Salvia × jamensis because no separate RHS cultivar rating for Magical® Mississippi was located.

visual: Compact tropical foliage plant with strongly variegated wavy leaves marbled white, light green and deep green, dark green margins and translucent purple colouring beneath.
water: Keep the compost consistently lightly moist but never waterlogged. Rainwater or filtered water is preferable where tap water is hard.
soil: Moisture-retentive but freely draining houseplant compost with added aeration such as perlite or fine bark.
soilWarning: Sensitive to waterlogging, cold draughts, dry air and harsh direct sunlight. Hard or mineral-rich water may contribute to brown leaf margins.
prune: No formal pruning required; remove damaged or ageing leaves cleanly at the base.
resilience: More vigorous and tolerant of higher light than its parent 'White Fusion', but still requires warm temperatures and relatively high humidity; spider mites and mealybugs can occur indoors.
uses: Houseplant, conservatory, bathroom, warm bright room and tropical foliage display.
uncertain: The original US plant patent names the cultivar Calathea lietzei 'Stella'. Kew now accepts Goeppertia lietzei as the botanical species name and treats Calathea lietzei as a synonym.
'Stella' originated as a naturally occurring mutation of 'Fusion White' and was selected for stronger foliage, increased vigour and improved tolerance of higher light.
The patent uses the spelling 'leitzei' in one formal species line, while Kew's accepted botanical spelling is lietzei.
